messages:
ella: Velora Labs opened a dispute — April invoice shows a 2.7M embed delta. They sent samples saying vendor normalization changed a metadata header which changed payload_sha but not actual vector bytes. Can finance triage if this is a credit?
ryan: interesting. so payload bytes identical but metadata changed -> different payload_sha. did you try a content-based dedupe (strip headers)?
ella: yep. quick SQL: 
```
select event_time, client, embed_count, source, payload_sha, content_hash from embed_ingest where client='velora_labs' and event_time between '2025-04-20 10:00' and '2025-04-20 10:20' limit 50;
```
sample rows:
"2025-04-20T10:05:02Z velora_labs 256 vendor-a 9f1a... 7b2c..."
"2025-04-20T10:05:02Z velora_labs 256 proxy    f2e3... 7b2c..."
"2025-04-20T10:05:03Z velora_labs 256 vendor-a 9f1a... 7b2c..."
ella: note content_hash is sha256 of the canonical vector bytes (strip headers/metadata). content_hash dedupe shows unique vectors = 142,500. raw accepted events = 2,842,700. duplicates by content_hash = 2,700,200. billing-bot: Automated alert: embed-content-dup-detect for velora_labs (confidence 0.91). Created ticket BILL-1119.
billing-bot: Note: payload_sha != content_hash for many rows; vendor changed metadata (trace-id/timestamp).
emily: unit price for Velora per contract = $0.00028. Preliminary credit = 2,700,200 * 0.00028 = $756.06. Recommend rounding to $756.
ryan: legal nuance: contract ties billing to accepted "events" with no content-normalization clause. But platform historically credited obvious duplicates where content identical. We should confirm with Legal for precedent.
lawrence: ops note: vendor-a released a patch on 2025-04-20 that included a request-id header; they said it shouldn't change payload. Looks like their serializer appended a microtimestamp. Vendor logs show increased retry loop earlier that day.
emily: can we produce an authoritative CSV mapping payload_sha -> content_hash with sample event_ids for the credit request?
ella: done. Created CREDIT-REQ-664 with CSV + mapping and content-normalization script used. Attached sample event_ids (first 100). Credit request linked to BILL-1119.
jessica: I'll spot-check 40 pairs from the CSV. If content_hash identical across multiple accepted events, I'll approve full credit. Please include the vendor advisory in the customer note.
ryan: also suggest a change to our ingest: compute content_hash at ingest (strip known headers) and use content_hash for short-window de-duplication (10s). Tagging eng-runtime.
lawrence: will open an engineering ticket ENG-rt-204 to compute content_hash and add dedupe window. Owner=lawrence, ETA 3w. Also will ask vendor-relations to push serializer guidance.
jessica: I spot-checked 40 samples, content_hash matches duplicates consistently. Approve $756 credit to Velora Labs. :+1:
ella: thanks — issuing adjustment invoice and sending customer note with explanation and vendor advisory. Rounding to $756 flat. Postmortem & ENG ticket linked. Closing after accounting posts credit. :white_check_mark:
